title: API Gateway
text: An API is a programming interface that allows access to a service, such as data or functionalities, provided by a third-party system. In this case, it is said that the third-party system exposes an API. If you want to learn more, I recommend checking out my dedicated video on APIs. The API Gateway, as its name suggests, is a device that acts as a gateway to allow external clients to use internal APIs and thus the services behind these APIs

title: API Gateway
text: . It saves clients from the burden of having to know the locations of each instance of the used service. They only need to contact the API Gateway. Here are some examples of API Gateway's. Google's APIG, API Management, AWS API Gateway, Azure API Gateway, and Kong API Gateway. The API Gateway performs various cross-cutting tasks. It's not an exhaustive list, but I'll present the main ones. Firstly, the API Gateway acts as a reverse proxy, routing client requests to the requested services

text: . Microservices can be called by clients through APIs. There is often confusion between API Gateway and Service Mesh. The main difference is that the API Gateway facilitates communication between external clients and services via their APIs, while the Service Mesh is a network service that facilitates communication between microservices internally.
